title: Solving Inverse Problems in Medical Imaging with Score-Based Generative Models
layout_note: Two panels split by a vertical dotted grey line. Left: a three-row grid of circled variables — sampled iterates (top), their measurement-corrected versions (middle) and noisy measurements (bottom) — running from the noise end at the left to the measurement y and a grey 'results' box at the right, with ellipses for the skipped steps. Right: one correction step drawn as data: the current iterate image is transformed into the measurement domain, combined with the measurement by masks (Λ, I − Λ, λΛ), summed and transformed back to the corrected image.
grouping: No containers around steps; the two kinds of process are separated by arrow colour only — black for unconditional generation, orange for measurement-driven steps — explained in a grey rounded legend box under the left panel. A small grey tag 'noise' marks the start of the chain.
shapes_depth: Variables are white circles with math labels (x̂_t, x̂'_t, ŷ_t). In the right panel the iterate and output are grayscale image thumbnails and the measurement-domain data are colour-mapped (magma) rectangles, three of them stacked in perspective as offset slabs where the masks combine; operators T, T^{-1}, P^{-1}(Λ) and the mask weights label the orange arrows; a black circled plus sums them.
proposed_highlight: Orange is reserved for everything the method adds to plain sampling (the measurement path and the correction), against black for the unconditional chain; the right panel expands that orange step with real data.
lesson: Separate the generative chain from the measurement correction purely by arrow colour (black vs orange, legend below), then open one correction step beside it as images that move into the measurement domain, get masked with y, and come back.
notes: venue ICLR 2022 from the PDF header ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2022') and the arXiv comment. The right panel's example data are CT images and sinograms, not MRI k-space; the paper covers both. Math in serif italic, labels sans.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: medical image reconstruction (sparse-view CT / undersampled MRI) via score-based sampling
taxonomy.note: the example data drawn are CT images and sinograms; the paper also covers MRI k-space

core.what: the reverse diffusion unrolled as a node lattice: a top row x̂_tN -> x̂_tN-1 -> ... -> x̂_t0 -> results in black, with an orange row of measurement-corrected nodes x̂' below it and an orange row of noised measurements ŷ_t fed from y underneath

relations.form: left panel: columns of circled variables per time step (x̂, x̂', ŷ) with ellipsis columns standing for the omitted steps, read left to right
at each step an orange arrow from ŷ_ti below and from x̂_ti above meet at x̂'_ti, which feeds diagonally into the next column's x̂
the same lattice carries both procedures: black arrows along the top row = unconditional generation, orange arrows = inverse-problem solving, keyed in a grey legend box
right of a dotted vertical rule, one step x̂_ti -> x̂'_ti is redrawn on data

the right panel draws the step on images: a CT slice is transformed by T into a colour-mapped sinogram, mixed with the measured sinogram via (1-λ)Λ, I-Λ and λΛ on labelled arrows, summed and mapped back by T^-1

channels.colour: arrow colour = procedure (black unconditional, orange inverse-problem solving), keyed; the sinograms keep their own magma colour map
channels.shape: circles = variables at a time step, rounded grey box = results, real images = the data in the zoom panel
channels.line: solid arrows only; the dotted vertical rule separates overview from detail
channels.frame: a grey tinted box marks the legend and the 'noise' tag

quality.strengths: the measurement-conditioning row is drawn as a second lattice under the unconditional chain so what is added reads as geometry; the zoomed step is drawn on real CT/sinogram images with the mixing weights as arrow labels rather than boxed formulas
quality.weaknesses: the orange arcs from y to ŷ_tN and ŷ_tN-1 sweep under the whole panel as the longest lines; the zoom panel is not tied to a specific step on the left; 'results' is an empty grey box

insights.structure: Two panels split by a vertical dotted grey line: left a three-row grid of circled variables (sampled x̂_t, corrected x̂'_t, noisy measurements ŷ_t) from 'noise' to a grey 'results' box with ellipsis columns; right one correction step opened up as data.
insights.data: Variables are white circles with serif math labels; in the right panel the iterate and output are grayscale CT thumbnails and the measurement-domain data are magma-coloured sinogram slabs, three stacked in perspective where masks Λ, I−Λ, λΛ combine.
insights.emphasis: Orange is reserved for everything the method adds (measurement path and correction) against black for unconditional generation, keyed in a grey legend box, and the right panel expands that orange step with real data.
insights.flow: Left panel runs right along the top chain, with orange arrows dropping and rising between rows and long orange curves sweeping from y back to every ŷ_t; right panel runs left to right T → mask combine → ⊕ → T^-1.
insights.avoid: The long orange curves from y back to ŷ_tN and ŷ_tN-1 run under the grid and crowd the legend box; the overlapping perspective slabs make which mask applies to which slab hard to read.

arrangement.units: an overview grid (left) and a zoom-in of one step (right), unframed and separated by a vertical dotted rule
arrangement.inputs_as: a small grey 'noise' tag at the top-left of the chain, with measurement y as a circled variable at the bottom right
arrangement.shared: the variables x̂_t, y and ŷ_t appear in both panels
